metaDescription: We evaluated six outdoor string lights on bulb shape, length, weatherproof rating, dimming and connectors to help you light a patio, deck or yard.
expertTake: The Brightown 100 ft ST38 string is our best overall pick for its commercial-grade wire, shatterproof Edison-style bulbs, IP65 rating and dimming support at a sensible tier. The GPATIO 100 ft G40 set is the value pick for classic globe bulbs with warm 2700K light. Anyone who wants colour effects or lights that stay up all year should look at Govee permanent lights, and those with no outlet should skip mains strings altogether.
introParagraphs: Outdoor string lights turn a patio, deck or pergola into a place you want to sit after dark. Done well, they give a soft, even glow that makes a space feel finished, and they cost little to run when the bulbs are LED.

Quality varies far more than the pictures suggest. Wire thickness, socket sealing, bulb material and the rated length that can be linked end to end decide whether a set survives a few winters or fails after one wet season.

products.name: Brightown 100 Ft ST38 Waterproof Dimmable String Lights
products.description:
The Brightown ST38 set runs 100 feet with 32 shatterproof Edison-style bulbs spaced about 3 feet apart, strung on commercial-grade wire. The listing gives it an IP65 waterproof rating and UL certification, and says the E12-base bulbs work with most dimmers, though a dimmer is not included. Sets can be connected end to end.

The tradeoff is spacing. Three feet between bulbs makes a more open, rustic look than the tight 2 foot spacing on the Brightown G40 set, so the glow is softer and less even. Compared with the GPATIO globe string, the ST38 bulb is longer and more vintage in style, and the filament-look LEDs are somewhat dimmer per bulb. It suits patios, pergolas and backyard canopies.

Check connections each season, keep sockets sealed, and avoid pulling the wire tight, because strain at the sockets is where water enters. Take the string down in extreme winter if you can, and replace any bulb that flickers promptly.
products.bestFor: Most patios and pergolas where a warm, vintage glow and reliable weatherproofing matter.
pros: IP65 rating and UL certification suit wet and snowy climates
Shatterproof ST38 bulbs survive drops and wind knocks
Commercial-grade wire holds the weight of long runs
Works with most dimmers via the E12 base
cons: Three foot spacing gives a more open, less even glow
Dimmer is not included in the box

products.name: GPATIO 100 Ft G40 LED String Lights, 2700K
products.description:
The GPATIO string is a 100 foot run with 36 G40 globe bulbs plus 2 spares, E12 bases and a 2700K warm white tone. The listing says it is ETL listed and has fully sealed sockets with an IP45 waterproof rating on heavy-duty wire. It is dimmable, and the shatterproof bulbs are meant for patios, gardens and weddings.

The tradeoff is the IP45 rating, which is a step below the IP65 on the Brightown string, so it handles rain splash but is less happy with driven spray or standing water at the sockets. Compared with the Brightown ST38, the G40 globe bulbs are rounder and give a classic party-light look. It is a good choice for a covered patio or a sheltered garden.

Check the sockets for water and keep the string clear of puddles. Keep a spare bulb handy, avoid overloading the connector chain, and store the string loosely coiled in the off season.
products.bestFor: Sheltered patios, weddings and gardens that want a classic globe look.
pros: Round G40 globe bulbs give a classic festive look
Warm 2700K colour is soft and flattering
Includes two spare bulbs for quick replacement
ETL listed with fully sealed sockets
cons: IP45 is weaker against driven rain than IP65 strings
Best kept under cover or in a sheltered position

products.name: Svater 105 Ft S14 Commercial Grade String Lights
products.description:
Svater's 105 foot set carries 33 S14 bulbs plus 2 spares, each a 1 watt LED putting out about 80 lumens on a standard E26 base. The string has a commercial-grade build, an IP65 waterproof rating and ETL certification for 120V outdoor use. It is dimmable with most dimmers, and the E26 base means you can swap in common bulbs.

The tradeoff is that the larger E26 base and S14 bulb are bulkier than E12 candelabra styles, so the look is chunkier. Compared with the Brightown ST38 set, the Svater uses a standard base, which makes replacements easier, but its bulbs are bigger. It suits cafes, decks and larger yards.

Check sockets and connectors each season, replace failed bulbs, and keep connections off the ground. Do not run more strings in series than the maker allows, and store coiled loosely.
products.bestFor: Larger decks and commercial-style patios that want standard replaceable bulbs.
pros: Standard E26 base makes bulb replacement easy
IP65 rating and ETL certification for outdoor use
Commercial-grade build handles long spans
Includes two spare bulbs
cons: Larger bulbs look chunkier than candelabra styles
Eighty lumens per bulb is soft for task lighting

products.name: Tenmiro 200 Ft S11 Edison LED String Lights
products.description:
The Tenmiro is a 200 foot string with 60 shatterproof S11 Edison-style bulbs, aimed at large yards, pool surrounds and long fences. At twice the length of most sets, it lets you span a big space without joining strings. The listing says the bulb shells are hard shatterproof plastic and the string is built to resist short circuits in rain.

The tradeoff is that long runs need support and careful power planning. Two hundred feet is heavy, and the wire needs a messenger cable or good anchor points to avoid sagging. Compared with the Brightown 100 ft, you get double the length from one plug, but you lose the clear IP65 and UL listing in the details. It suits large yards where joining shorter sets would be awkward.

Check the whole run for sagging after storms, inspect sockets and keep the plug sheltered. Test the string after taking it down and before hanging.
products.bestFor: Large yards, pool areas and long fence lines that need one long run.
pros: Two hundred feet covers a large area from one plug
Sixty shatterproof bulbs reduce breakage worries
Edison style gives a warm vintage look
Waterproof design is built for outdoor weather
cons: Long, heavy runs need strong anchor points or a cable
Ratings are less detailed than IP65 listed rivals

products.name: Govee Permanent Outdoor Lights Pro, 200 Ft RGBIC
products.description:
The Govee Pro is a different kind of outdoor light: 200 feet of permanent, app-controlled RGBIC LEDs with 120 lights, 75 scene modes and warm and cold white settings for everyday use. A new anti-glare lens gives a cleaner light shape, and the string is cuttable and spliceable so you can fit it to your roofline.

The tradeoff is that it is a roofline and accent system, not a cosy patio festoon. It costs more than a basic string, and needs a smartphone app and Wi-Fi or Bluetooth to get the full effect. Compared with the Brightown string, it provides colour and scene control but no classic bulb look. It suits holiday decorating and year-round roofline accents.

Install it with the supplied clips, keep the controller dry and update the firmware when prompted. Check the clips each season, and avoid cutting except at marked points.
products.bestFor: Roofline accents, holiday displays and colour effects that stay up all year.
pros: Seventy-five scenes and colour control for holidays and events
Warm and cold whites work for everyday accent light
Cuttable and spliceable to fit custom roofline lengths
Designed to stay up year round
cons: Needs an app and wireless connection for full control
Not the cosy bulb-string look of a patio festoon

products.name: MGVIH 100 Ft ST38 Dimmable String Lights with Remote
products.description:
The MGVIH is a 100 foot string with 37 ST38 shatterproof bulbs plus 2 spares and a remote control that steps brightness through 25, 50, 75 and 100 percent. The bulbs are made of impact-resistant PET and use an E12 base. It is meant for patios, decks and gardens.

The tradeoff is that the remote adds a point of failure, and the listing gives less detail on the weather rating than the Brightown. Compared with the Brightown ST38, it has five more bulbs and a built-in remote, but a less proven weatherproofing story. It suits people who want to control brightness from a chair without buying a separate dimmer.

Keep the remote battery fresh, check the sockets and connectors, and store the remote indoors. Replace a failed bulb with the spare.
products.bestFor: Patio users who want brightness control from a remote rather than a wall dimmer.
pros: Remote steps brightness through four levels
Thirty-seven bulbs and two spares give a full run
Impact-resistant PET bulbs survive drops
No separate dimmer is needed
cons: Remote adds a battery and a possible failure point
Weatherproof detail is less documented than rivals

buyingCriteria.explanation: IP ratings tell you how the sockets cope with water. IP65 handles driven rain and snow, as on the Brightown and Svater, while IP45 on the GPATIO suits sheltered spots. Non-rated strings often fail after one wet season. Check the rating on the plug and the sockets, not just the wire.

G40 globes give a classic party look, ST38 and S11 give a vintage Edison filament look, and S14 gives a larger, chunkier shape. Bulb size affects spacing and glow, so match style to how formal or rustic your space is.

Total length and bulb spacing decide how many strings you need. A 100 ft set with 3 ft spacing has fewer bulbs than a 55 ft set with 2 ft spacing. Measure your span and add slack for drooping, because a string pulled tight stresses the sockets.

A 2700K warm white feels cosy, while cooler whites feel harsh outdoors. Bulbs of about 80 lumens, like the Svater, give soft ambient light. For task lighting such as a grill area, add a separate spotlight instead of relying on string bulbs.

Dimmable bulbs make the lights flexible, but you need a compatible dimmer, as the Brightown notes, or a built-in remote like the MGVIH. Smart systems like the Govee add app control and scenes. Decide how much control you want before paying for it.

Long strings sag, and sagging stresses sockets. Use hooks, a messenger wire or posts every few feet. The Tenmiro at 200 feet especially needs strong anchors. Plan your power source and keep plugs under cover.

specDecoder.meaning: A code for dust and water ingress. IP65 withstands jets of water, while IP45 handles splashes.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Brightown and Svater list IP65, while the GPATIO lists IP45 for its sockets.

specDecoder.meaning: E12 is a small candelabra base and E26 is the standard household base. Standard bases are easier to replace.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Svater uses E26, while the Brightown, GPATIO and MGVIH use E12.

specDecoder.meaning: Measured in kelvin, lower numbers are warmer. Around 2700K is a warm white typical for patio lighting.
specDecoder.watchFor: The GPATIO lists 2700K, while other strings leave the figure out.

specDecoder.meaning: How bright each bulb is. Patio string bulbs are usually decorative, not task lights.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Svater lists about 80 lumens per 1 watt bulb.

specDecoder.meaning: UL or ETL marks mean the electrical design was assessed for safety. They are a basic quality check.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Brightown lists UL certification and the GPATIO and Svater list ETL.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weatherproofing and certification
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared IP ratings and UL or ETL listings from published specifications. IP65 strings like the Brightown scored highest. Strings with vague waterproof claims were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bulb quality and style
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at bulb material, shape and base. Shatterproof PET bulbs earned credit. We noted the visual difference between G40, ST38, S11 and S14 shapes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Length and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked total length, bulb count and spacing. The Tenmiro at 200 feet gives the longest single run. We favoured sets that match typical patio spans.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and dimming
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared dimmer support, remote controls and smart features. The MGVIH remote and Govee app offer built-in control. Strings needing a separate dimmer were noted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Durability and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We used owner feedback patterns to spot weak sockets and thin wire. Commercial-grade wire and sealed sockets earned credit. Extras without a physical benefit were not rewarded.

maintenance.why: Water enters at sockets and plugs first. Reseal or replace any that look cracked.
Sag stresses sockets and can pull hooks free. Re-tension or add supports.
A dead bulb can break the circuit on some strings. Keep spares handy.
Plugs are the weakest point for water. Use a weatherproof cover or outlet box.
Tight bends crack the wire. A loose coil in a dry box keeps the string intact.

faq.q: Are G40 or Edison bulbs better for outdoor string lights?
faq.a: Neither is better, they are different looks. G40 globes feel festive, while Edison bulbs feel vintage. Choose by style and check the weatherproof rating. Install hooks or eye screws every few feet and run a thin steel messenger wire first, then clip the lights to it so the wire carries the weight. Without support, long runs droop and pull on the sockets. Leave a gentle curve rather than pulling taut, because wind and temperature changes make the wire move.

faq.q: How much should I spend on outdoor string lights?
faq.a: A basic set costs little, but poorly sealed sets fail within a season. Spend a bit more for IP65 and certified sockets, and more still for smart features. Check the maximum run in the manual, because it is set by the wire gauge and the total wattage. Plugging in more than the maker allows can overheat the wire or trip a breaker. When you need to cover more distance, use a second outlet or a weatherproof extension cord rather than chaining past the limit.

faq.q: How long do outdoor string lights last?
faq.a: Good LED strings can last several seasons. Sockets and connectors are the failure points, not the LEDs, so inspect them every year. Warm white around 2700K is the usual choice for patios, because it flatters skin and wood and feels relaxed in the evening. Cooler white looks harsher and can make a garden feel like a car park. If you need brighter working light, add a separate fixture instead of switching the string to a cool tone.

faq.q: Can I leave outdoor string lights up all year?
faq.a: Only if they are designed for it, like the Govee permanent lights. Standard patio strings handle weather but wear faster if left up through winter.

faq.q: Is it safe to connect multiple strings?
faq.a: Yes, but only up to the maximum run the maker lists, since too many strings overload the wire. Use a weatherproof outlet and keep plugs off the ground.
Not necessarily, but dimming lets you set a softer mood and lower glare. Check that your dimmer is compatible with LED bulbs, or choose a set with a remote.
